answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 6 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The pigment multiplier is published, charged in opal, and mirror lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3030 identities would post 2088 proofs and burn roughly 78 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
